title: MileageTracker
summary: A Kotlin Android app for mileage, vehicle records, receipts, and exports. Local trip storage and recovery are central, with optional cloud sync and a sanitized public repository.
problem: Drivers need a dependable way to record trip details, organize mileage, and review information for their own records without losing sight of incomplete or unverified entries.
role: Solo developer building the Android application and maintaining its verification and closed-beta checklist.
accomplishments: Built an Android workflow for captured trips, business or personal classification, vehicle records, and report/export actions.
Implemented local tracking checkpoints and retry paths to support interrupted-trip recovery independently of cloud connectivity.
Added unit and Android UI coverage; the approved recordings demonstrate current screens while device and release gates remain open.
stakeholders: Drivers recording personal or business mileage
currentStatus: Closed-beta solo foundation with a sanitized public source repository. Device validation and release gates remain; it is not a general release.
publicationBoundary: The supplied screen recordings and sanitized source repository are approved for public display. Reporting features are designed to support recordkeeping; no CRA acceptance is promised.
limitations: The project remains a closed-beta foundation with release gates still tracked.
No tax advice or CRA-acceptance promise is made.
The public screen recordings show owner-approved real trip, profile, and vehicle information; they do not change the project's closed-beta status.
The linked README uses CRA compliance language. This portfolio does not establish an independent compliance assessment or CRA acceptance.
claimPolicy: Do not describe the project as fully released or generally available.
Do not promise CRA acceptance or present the app as tax advice.
The owner approved the five supplied recordings, including the visible account email, trip records, and vehicle details, for public display.
evidence: Automated unit and Android UI coverage spans validation, interrupted-trip recovery, synchronization, authentication, exports, and core screens.
A closed-beta checklist separates implemented features, known blockers, device smoke tests, emulator-rule checks, and release gates.
Sanitized public source, architecture documentation, and a guided codebase tour are linked below.

sections.heading: The problem and my role
paragraphs: Drivers need more than a distance total: trips need context, vehicles need accurate odometer records, and reports need entries that can be reviewed. I am the solo developer, responsible for the Android implementation, supporting services, verification work, and beta-readiness checklist.

The scope includes GPS trip capture, business or personal classification, multiple vehicles, annual odometer records, expense and receipt capture, and PDF/CSV reporting. The aim is useful Canadian mileage recordkeeping, with incomplete entries and release limitations kept visible.

sections.heading: Architecture: screens through use cases to storage
paragraphs: Jetpack Compose screens receive StateFlow state from Hilt-injected view models. Use cases and repository interfaces separate business behavior from Room, DataStore, and Firebase implementations. Room owns local records; optional synchronization goes through an outbox rather than direct screen-to-cloud writes.

sections.heading: Durability before connectivity
paragraphs: Tracking checkpoints the active session, then buffers a completed trip before persistence. WorkManager retries local writes independently of network access; cloud synchronization requires connectivity and consent. Keeping those paths separate supports recovery when a drive or connection is interrupted.

sections.heading: The application in the recordings
paragraphs: The five recordings on this page show the dashboard, automatically captured trips awaiting classification, the trip-detail form, manual tracking controls, vehicle settings, and reports. On the Trips screen, swipe left or right to classify a trip as business or personal, or select it to edit its details in a form. Captions and written descriptions explain each recording.
bullets: The overview shows a suggested trip classification and editable fields.
The Trips screen lists automatically captured, unclassified trips; selecting a trip opens its editable details and classification controls.
The tracking clip shows controls in their ready state; it does not demonstrate a completed drive.
Vehicle and report clips show their respective screens, rather than proving every background or export path.

sections.heading: Verification and the remaining release work
paragraphs: The project includes unit and Android UI coverage for validation, interrupted-trip recovery, synchronization, authentication, exports, and core screens. A beta checklist distinguishes implementation evidence from device smoke tests and release approval.

Physical-device tracking validation, complete synchronization coverage, Firebase and Google Play configuration, and release signing remain release gates. Team workflows and accounting integrations are disabled prototypes. Automated test results from the newly sanitized copy have not been re-run as part of this portfolio update.

sections.heading: Public source, with configuration kept separate
paragraphs: The public repository is a sanitized copy with a fresh history, placeholder configuration, and a renamed example package ID. Its README documents the setup needed for a developer to supply their own configuration. The architecture and onboarding guides offer a route from the visible screens into the code.
